arxiv-1805-07923.title: Multi-Level Spectral Deferred Corrections Scheme for the Shallow Water Equations on the Rotating Sphere
arxiv-1805-07923.creator: François P. Hamon, Martin Schreiber, Michael L. Minion
arxiv-1805-07923.description: Abstract Efficient time integration schemes are necessary to capture the complex processes involved in atmospheric flows over long periods of time. In this work, we propose a high-order, implicit-explicit numerical scheme that combines Multi-Level Spectral Deferred Corrections (MLSDC) and the Spherical Harmonics (SH) transform to solve the wave-propagation problems arising from the shallow-water equations on the rotating sphere.

arxiv-2103-15351.title: Rank Minimization-based Toeplitz Reconstruction for DoA Estimation Using Coprime Array Thanks: This work was supported in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant Nos. 62001103, U1936201 and the Basic Research Program of Jiangsu Province under Grant No. BK20190338. (Corre
arxiv-2103-15351.creator: Shengheng Liu, Zihuan Mao
arxiv-2103-15351.description: Abstract In this paper, we address the problem of direction finding using coprime array, which is one of the most preferred sparse array configurations. Motivated by the fact that non-uniform element spacing hinders full utilization of the underlying information in the receive signals, we propose a direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation algorithm based on low-rank reconstruction of the Toeplitz covariance matrix.

arxiv-2109-02869.title: The Sensory Neuron as a Transformer: Permutation-Invariant Neural Networks for Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2109-02869.creator: Yujin TangGoogle Brain yujintang@google.com, David HaGoogle Brain hadavid@google.com
arxiv-2109-02869.description: Abstract In complex systems, we often observe complex global behavior emerge from a collection of agents interacting with each other in their environment, with each individual agent acting only on locally available information, without knowing the full picture. Such systems have inspired development of artificial intelligence algorithms in areas such as swarm optimization and cellular automata.

arxiv-2209-12610.title: Relativistic orbits of S2 star in the presence of scalar field Preprint: RUP-22-20, AP-GR-183, NITEP 146
arxiv-2209-12610.creator: Parth Bambhaniya, Ashok B. Joshi, Dipanjan Dey, Pankaj S. Joshi, Arindam Mazumdar, Tomohiro Harada, Ken-ichi Nakao
arxiv-2209-12610.description: Abstract The general theory of relativity predicts the relativistic effect in the orbital motions of S-stars which are orbiting around our Milky-way galactic center. The post-Newtonian or higher-order approximated Schwarzschild black hole models have been used by GRAVITY and UCLA galactic center groups to carefully investigate the S2 star’s periastron precession.

arxiv-2405-02510.title: Low-cost sensors and circuits for plasma education: characterizing power and illuminance Note: Research supported in part by the Brazilian agency CNPq Grant 305158/2017-1; 305998/2020-0; 421486/2016-3.
arxiv-2405-02510.creator: Alessandro N. Vargas, Victor Miller, Ali Mesbah, Gabriele Neretti
arxiv-2405-02510.description: Abstract Industrial applications of plasma have significantly increased beyond semiconductor manufacturing in recent years. This necessitates training a skilled workforce in plasma science and technology. However, an essential challenge to this end stems from the high cost of plasma devices and diagnostics. The limited access to plasma devices has hindered plasma education, particularly in the least developed countries.

arxiv-2412-05472.title: Detection of Surface Waves During Femtosecond Filamentation
arxiv-2412-05472.creator: Travis Garrett, Anna Janicek, J. Todd Fayard II, Jennifer Elle
arxiv-2412-05472.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Travis Garrett, Anna Janicek, J. Todd Fayard II, Jennifer Elle. Ultrashort pulsed lasers (USPL) can produce thin columns of plasma in air via femtosecond filamentation, and these plasmas have been found to generate broadband TeraHertz (THz) and Radio Frequency (RF) radiation.

arxiv-2509-15850.title: Parabolic Normalizers in Finite Coxeter Groups as Subdirect Products Thanks: The authors would like to thank their charming wives for their unwavering support during the preparation of this paper.
arxiv-2509-15850.creator: J. Matthew Douglass, Götz Pfeiffer, Gerhard Röhrle
arxiv-2509-15850.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by J. Matthew Douglass, Götz Pfeiffer, Gerhard Röhrle. We revisit the structure of the normalizer N W ​ ( P ) N_{W}(P) of a parabolic subgroup P P in a finite Coxeter group W W , originally described by Howlett. Building on Howlett’s Lemma, which provides canonical complements for reflection subgroups, and inspired by a recent construction of Serre for involution centralizers, we refine this understanding by interpreting N W ​ ( P ) N_{W}(P) as a subdirect product via Goursat’s Lemma.

arxiv-2512-13711.title: Delete and Retain: Efficient Unlearning for Document Classification
arxiv-2512-13711.creator: Aadya Goel, Mayuri Sridhar, [-1em] Acton-Boxborough Regional High School MIT
arxiv-2512-13711.description: Abstract Machine unlearning aims to efficiently remove the influence of specific training data from a model without full retraining. While much progress has been made in unlearning for LLMs, document classification models remain relatively understudied. In this paper, we study class-level unlearning for document classifiers and present Hessian Reassignment, a two-step, model-agnostic solution.

pmc-11689698.title: EXAMINING THE ROLE OF SOUTHERN CONTEXT FOR DEMENTIA, DISABILITY, AND MORTALITY AMONG OLDER US BLACKS AND WHITES
pmc-11689698.creator: Jaein Kim, Hyungmin Cha, Mateo Farina, Mark D Hayward
pmc-11689698.description: Racial inequalities in older adult health are well-documented. Compared to Whites, Blacks have greater risks of disability, dementia, multimorbidity and mortality. These differences in age-related health are paralleled by race differences in context. In particular, approximately 80% of older Blacks were born in Jim Crow South no matter where they currently live compared to 30% percent of older Whites.

pmc-12553563.title: Plasma IL-6, IL-8 and IL-10 as predictors of response to PD-1 blockade immunochemotherapy in advanced gastric cancer
pmc-12553563.creator: Fumeng Yang, Juncun Yao, Xinyue Tong, Xuan Luo, Qian Liu, Wei Zhu
pmc-12553563.description: Although immunotherapy has demonstrated clinical efficacy in advanced gastric cancer (AGC), its therapeutic benefits are limited to a subset of patients. This study aimed to evaluate circulating cytokines as potential prognostic biomarkers to enhance the precision of clinical decision-making in PD-1 inhibitor-based immunotherapy for AGC.

pmc-12689121.title: Post-operative seroma formation following laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12689121.creator: Sunil Basukala, Sunischit Chandra Neupane, Sulav Neupane, Sujan Tamang, Niranjan Thapa, Oshan Shrestha
pmc-12689121.description: Background:Seroma formation is the most frequent complication after laparoscopic hernia repair, and there are reports of seroma being mistaken for recurrences, with the correct diagnosis being made only after groin exploration. Laparoscopic hernia repair, first introduced by LeBlanc and Booth in 1993, has gained increasing popularity over time.

pmc-12788558.title: Efficacy of Silver Diamine Fluoride and Nanosilver Fluoride in Preventing Caries: A Comparative Study
pmc-12788558.creator: Priyatam Karade, Sameep Singh, Neeti Mittal, Bismay Singh, Ashtha Arya, Preeti Patil, Jnana Ranjan Swain
pmc-12788558.description: Background:Dental caries remains a prevalent global health issue, particularly among children. Silver diamine fluoride (SDF) is a well-established caries-arresting agent, while nanosilver fluoride (NSF), a newer formulation combining silver nanoparticles and fluoride, offers potential antibacterial and remineralizing benefits. However, comparative evidence on their caries-preventive efficacy remains limited.

pmc-13188355.title: Losartan to Improve Outcomes after multi-ligament kNee injury (LION Trial)
pmc-13188355.creator: Sean Kehoe, Austin Stone, Xiaoning Yuan, Caitlin Conley, Gregory Hawk, Stacy Smith, Molly Zgoda, Natalie Corey, Darren Johnson, Benjamin Wilson, Liang Zhou, Eric Berkson, Simon Goertz, Logan Huff, Ian Hutchinson, Elizabeth Matzkin, Lars Richardson, Christian Lattermann, Cale Jacobs
pmc-13188355.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMulti-ligament knee injuries (MLKI) are complex injury patterns that affect two or more ligaments of the knee. Although surgical intervention can improve functional and clinical outcomes, a large percentage of patients are unable to return to preoperative activity levels. One reason for this is loss of knee range of motion (ROM), which characterizes the exaggerated pro-inflammatory environment of arthrofibrosis and is associated with future osteoarthritis risk.

pmc-13218827.title: Feasibility and Safety of a Computer-Controlled Device for Transradial Cerebral Angiography: A Prospective Pilot Study
pmc-13218827.creator: Shun Tanaka, Koji Hirata, Koichi Uramaru, Hideaki Matsumura, Takeshi Yoshimoto, Hisayuki Hosoo, Yoshiro Ito, Mikito Hayakawa, Aiki Marushima, Hiroshi Yamagami, Yuji Matsumaru
pmc-13218827.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of a computer-controlled local anesthetic delivery device during transradial cerebral angiography and to descriptively assess procedural pain and hemodynamic changes in an initial series of patients.MethodsIn this prospective pilot study, 10 consecutive adult patients undergoing elective diagnostic cerebral angiography via the radial artery received local anesthesia with a computer-controlled injection device using 1 mL of 3% mepivacaine delivered through a 33-G needle.

pmc-13260316.creator: Suman Ranjit, Belen Torrado, Alexander Vallmitjana, Amanda Fedyk Durkin, Alexander Dvornikov, Anand Ganesan, Kristen M Kelly, Mihaela Balu

pmc-13592950.title: Prognostic value of the HALP (hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet) score in emergency versus elective inguinal hernia repair
pmc-13592950.creator: Mehmet Zeki Öğüt, Onur Ağ, Nizamettin Kutluer, Bekir Saricik, Tamer Gündoğdu, Ayşe Azak Bozan, Ümit Karatepe, Mehmet Buğra Bozan
pmc-13592950.description: The hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score is a novel prognostic biomarker that reflects a patient’s immune-nutritional status. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic value of the HALP score in patients undergoing emergency versus elective inguinal hernia repair. This retrospective study analyzed data from 235 patients who underwent inguinal hernia surgery at a single center.

pmc-13675750.title: Rethinking the Platinum Standard in SCLC: A Meta-Analysis of Limited- and Extensive-Stage Disease in the Immunotherapy Era
pmc-13675750.creator: Tomer Meirson, Hadas Ditzian Kugler, Ekaterina Hanovich, Ofer Rotem, Mor Moskovitz, Ari Raphael
pmc-13675750.description: IntroductionSCLC is an aggressive malignancy for which platinum-based chemotherapy is the cornerstone of treatment. Although immunotherapy has redefined the standard of care, the optimal choice between cisplatin and carboplatin remains debated. This study evaluated the impact of platinum backbone selection on survival outcomes across the SCLC spectrum in the immunotherapy era.
